info.title: backend HTTP API
info.description: JSON API served under /api/v1 plus two unauthenticated probes at the root. Protected routes expect `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`; refresh tokens travel only in httpOnly cookies. All examples use fake values.

post.description: Registers a PERSON or ORG user from an e-imzo signed challenge. The refresh token is set as the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie (path `/api/v1/auth`); it is never returned in the body.

post.summary: Log in with a password (PERSON/ORG only)
post.description: The identifier is an email or a phone number. Every failure returns the same generic 401 (no user enumeration). Repeated failed attempts lock the (identifier, source IP) pair, and a higher all-IP threshold briefly locks the identifier itself; a locked attempt returns 429 before the credentials are checked, identically whether or not the account exists. A SYSTEM account is never authenticated here. Sets the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie.

post.summary: Log in with an e-imzo signature
post.description: Every failure returns the same generic 401. Sets the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie.

post.summary: Select the workspace for a pending person token
post.description: Requires a pending-workspace access token (PERSON or SYSTEM). Sets the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie. An inactive organization is rejected with 403.

post.summary: Switch the workspace for a selected person token

get.summary: List the current person's available workspaces
get.description: Returns the active organizations owned by the person behind the access token's uid claim — exactly the workspace_options a PERSON login returns — plus which workspace the token is currently in. PERSON tokens only (personal or org workspace); a pending-selection token and ORG/SYSTEM tokens are rejected.

post.summary: Rotate the session from the refresh cookie
post.description: Reads the httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie (path `/api/v1/auth`); no Authorization header is required (an expired access token must still be refreshable). A `system_refresh_token` is rejected here. Sets a rotated `refresh_token` cookie. The session also enforces server-side limits: it is rejected with the same 401 once idle for longer than REFRESH_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES or once its total lifetime exceeds SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MAX_MINUTES (measured from the session's first token), and the rotated cookie's Expires never exceeds that absolute cap. A refresh presenting a token that was rotated moments ago — a second browser tab racing on the same shared cookie — within REFRESH_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS is NOT treated as reuse: it returns a fresh access token but sets no new refresh cookie (the winning rotation already set it). Reuse outside that window, or any revoked/expired token, returns 401. Cookie-based endpoints cannot be exercised reliably from the Swagger UI Try-it-out (cookies are managed by the browser).

Revokes the refresh-token family from the `refresh_token` cookie, clears the cookie and denies the presented access token's jti for its remaining lifetime. Works without an access token (the bearer is optional and only trusted when its signature validates). Idempotent.

Revokes every refresh-token family for the caller and denies the caller's own access token's jti. Clears the `refresh_token` cookie. Other devices' access tokens remain valid until they expire (up to ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES).

Authenticates only user_type=SYSTEM accounts. Unknown email, wrong password, inactive account, a non-SYSTEM account and a missing email/password hash all return the same generic 401. Uses a dedicated fail-closed per-IP limiter plus a per-(email, IP) lockout (429). Sets the httpOnly `system_refresh_token` cookie (path `/api/v1/system/auth`), which is not interchangeable with `refresh_token`.

Reads the httpOnly `system_refresh_token` cookie (path `/api/v1/system/auth`). A `refresh_token` is rejected here with a generic failure. The session also enforces server-side limits: it is rejected with the same 401 once idle for longer than SYSTEM_REFRESH_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES or once its total lifetime exceeds SYSTEM_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MAX_MINUTES (measured from the session's first token), and the rotated cookie's Expires never exceeds that absolute cap. A refresh presenting a token rotated moments ago within REFRESH_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS returns a fresh access token but sets no new refresh cookie (the winning rotation already set it). Reuse outside that window, or any revoked/expired token, returns 401. Cookie-based endpoint; cannot be exercised reliably from Try-it-out.

Requires a valid SYSTEM access token. Revokes the refresh token(s), clears the `system_refresh_token` cookie and denies the access token's jti (fail-closed: if the denylist write fails it returns 500 so the caller can retry). Idempotent.

post.description: Rotates the password of the user identified by the access token's uid claim. current_password is verified against the stored bcrypt hash; wrong values are counted per user and the account is locked for ACCOUNT_PW_LOCKOUT_SEC after ACCOUNT_PW_MAX_FAILURES failures — the lockout is checked before the password is compared, so a locked attempt returns the same 429 whether or not the password is correct. The new password must differ from the current one and follow the 8-72 byte rule. On success every other refresh-token family is revoked; the caller's current session survives only when the httpOnly refresh_token cookie identifies it (its path /api/v1/auth covers this route), otherwise all families, including the current one, are revoked. PERSON and ORG principals only: SYSTEM is rejected with 403. An account without a password (e-imzo-only) is rejected with 409.

Starts (or resends) the email change for the user identified by the access token's uid claim; calling this endpoint again is the resend. current_password is verified like the password change (wrong password 401, locked 429 checked before the comparison). The new address must differ from the current one and must not already belong to another account (409, checked here and again on confirm). A 6-digit code from crypto/rand is stored only as an HMAC and sent to the NEW address; it expires in EMAIL_CODE_TTL_SEC and at most EMAIL_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS wrong codes invalidate the pending change. A repeat request within EMAIL_CODE_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SEC is 429, and per-user, per-target-address and per-IP hourly and daily send caps also apply (429, fail-closed on a Redis outage). If the code email cannot be sent the request returns 500 and never reports success, while the cooldown still applies. No raw address or code is ever logged. PERSON and ORG only: SYSTEM is rejected with 403. An account without a password is rejected with 409.

202.description: Verification code sent to the new address.

post.description: Completes the pending email change for the user identified by the access token's uid claim. The code is compared in constant time against the stored HMAC; a wrong code, an expired code, exhausted attempts and no pending change all return the same 400 (never 401, which the frontend treats as session expiry). Uniqueness of the new address is re-checked inside the transaction that updates the row, and the partial unique index is the final guard; a conflict returns 409 and consumes the pending change. On success email_verified_at is set, the pending state is cleared, an audit entry is written (masked values only) and a notice is sent to the OLD address (skipped silently when the account had none). Returns the refreshed profile. PERSON and ORG only: SYSTEM is rejected with 403.

post.description: Blocks a PERSON/ORG account. Writes the user not-before marker first, then deactivates the account, revokes its refresh-token families and audits. A Redis failure aborts with 503 and no database change. A SYSTEM target is refused with 422; use /admin/system-users/{uuid}/block instead.

422.description: The target account is a SYSTEM user; block it through /admin/system-users/{uuid}/block.

post.summary: Revoke all sessions of a user
post.description: Revokes a PERSON/ORG user's sessions: writes the not-before marker, then revokes every refresh-token family. Does not change is_active. A Redis failure aborts with 503 and no database change. A SYSTEM target is refused with 422; use /admin/system-users/{uuid}/sessions/revoke instead.

422.description: The target account is a SYSTEM user; revoke it through /admin/system-users/{uuid}/sessions/revoke.

post.description: Reactivates a PERSON/ORG account. Does not delete the not-before marker. A SYSTEM target is refused with 422; use /admin/system-users/{uuid}/unblock instead.

422.description: The target account is a SYSTEM user; unblock it through /admin/system-users/{uuid}/unblock.

post.description: Blocks a SYSTEM account. Requires system.role.manage, which system_support does not hold. Writes the user not-before marker first, then deactivates the account, revokes its refresh-token families and audits. A Redis failure aborts with 503 and no database change. The last active system_admin cannot be blocked.
Reactivates a SYSTEM account. Requires system.role.manage. Does not delete the not-before marker.

post.summary: Revoke all sessions of a SYSTEM user
post.description: Revokes a SYSTEM account's sessions. Requires system.role.manage, which system_support does not hold. Writes the not-before marker, then revokes every refresh-token family and audits. Does not change is_active. A Redis failure aborts with 503 and no database change. Revoking your own sessions is refused.

get.description: Requires a SYSTEM principal. No permission is required: a caller may always describe itself. roles and permissions are the grants resolved for this request; the response exposes only the external uuid.

200.description: The caller's identity and resolved grants.

bearerAuth.description: PERSON, ORG or SYSTEM access token.

LangQuery.name: lang
LangQuery.description: Response language. Resolution order when omitted: Accept-Language, then the active default language (uz).

IncludeTranslationsQuery.name: include_translations
IncludeTranslationsQuery.description: When true, include the full translations map.

LimitQuery.name: limit
LimitQuery.description: Page size. Default 20, maximum 100 (employees: default 50, maximum 200).

IfNoneMatchHeader.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatchHeader.description: ETag from a previous response; a match returns 304.

AcceptLanguageHeader.name: Accept-Language
AcceptLanguageHeader.description: Used when ?lang= is absent to pick the response language; falls back to the active default language.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid credentials/token. Login-style endpoints intentionally return a single generic 401 for every failure reason (unknown account, wrong password, inactive account, non-matching user type).

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not permitted (wrong principal type, or an unresolved user/tenant).

RequestEntityTooLarge.description: Request body exceeded the 2 MiB limit.

message.description: Human-readable error message (or null for a successful delete).

access_token.description: JWT access token. The refresh token is delivered only as an httpOnly cookie, never in the body.

workspace_options.description: Present when the caller must still choose a workspace. Only active organizations are listed.
Active organizations owned by the current person; identical to the workspace_options returned by login.

workspace.description: The workspace the presented token is scoped to.

org_id.description: External UUID of the active org when workspace is org, otherwise null.

translation.description: Translation for the resolved language, if any.

translations.description: All translations, present only when include_translations=true.

target_type.description: Subject kind (for example user or org); empty when the event has no single subject.

target_uuid.description: External UUID of the subject the event changed.

TranslationBundle.description: One map of key/value pairs per requested page slug.

language_code.description: Optional; an empty/unknown/inactive code falls back to the default language.

org_id.description: Required when workspace=org, forbidden when workspace=personal.

UserMe.description: The caller's own user row, narrowed to non-sensitive fields (no internal id, password hash or flags).

email_verified_at.description: When the email address was confirmed through the change flow; null for accounts that never completed it (including every pre-existing account).

current_password.description: Verified against the stored bcrypt hash.

new_password.description: Must differ from the current password and satisfy the 8-72 byte rule.

new_email.description: Trimmed before validation. Must differ from the current address and must not be used by another account.

current_password.description: Verified against the stored bcrypt hash.

code.description: The 6-digit code sent to the new address.

expires_in.description: Seconds the verification code stays valid.

resend_after.description: Seconds until the change request may be repeated.

language_code.description: Must match an active language code.

AdminUser.description: A PERSON/ORG account on the admin surface. External UUID only; never the internal bigint id.

AdminMe.description: The authenticated SYSTEM caller: external UUID plus the roles and permission codes resolved for this request.
